research.summary:
The latest OpenCode is 2.3.0, released 2026-11-13 as npm `@opencode/cli` from anomalyco/opencode. The V1 line still ships separately as `opencode-ai` (latest 1.19.5), and both install an `opencode` command. OpenCode is not installed on this machine, so nothing was run; every fact below comes from the npm registry, the v2 docs (opencode.ai/v2/*.md) or v2.3.0 source on GitHub.

Upstream 157efde is V1-only and breaks on V2 in three verified places:
- It configures the plugin as a single .mjs file. V2 skips any configured plugin path that is not a directory, so turn-end reports never arrive.
- It passes `--model` to the full-screen TUI, which in V2 has no such flag (only `run` and `mini` do).
- It uses the shared background service. With several agents, each agent's config and notify URL leak through the first agent's server unless every session runs with `--standalone`.

Smaller stale points: the V1 config keys (`plugin`, `permission`, a flat `mcp`, `provider` with `npm`, `autoupdate`) still load but are deprecated. `autoupdate` in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT does nothing, because the V2 updater reads only global config files. V2 MCP servers default to Code Mode. V2 reads only AGENTS.md, never CLAUDE.md.

Fork comparison:
- rosariomoscato/droidsembly (8adf85b, fa4e3fa, b10b23b, f99c760) matches v2.3.0 best. It uses native V2 config (`plugins` with options, `mcp.servers` with codemode false, `agents`, `providers` with `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible`, ordered `permissions`). It also runs `--standalone`, assigns its own `ses_` session IDs (filtered exactly in the plugin), listens to `session.execution.*` events and requires 2.x. It sits on top of #311 and 157efde and has the most tests, but it is mixed in with telemetry, i18n, branding and Box work, so it has to be extracted, not cherry-picked.
- mysteryreloaded (778ed82, 625cee7, 7d1a0ce, 8dc1d0c) is the smallest correct shape: `--standalone`, a plugin folder exporting `{ id, setup }`, and the model set in config. But its base predates #311 (conflicts in the opencode launch branch and its tests), it keeps V1 keys, guesses the root session as "the first one seen", and listens for `session.error`, which is not on v2.3.0's public event stream. As a result failed turns are never reported as TurnError.
- Calel33 (273479d and the rest) supports V1 and V2 side by side, which contradicts D-001. It does not use `--standalone` (breaks with several agents), does not filter child sessions, and is based on 961bce6, before #311. Its off-PATH CLI lookup and its effort-to-`#variant` mapping are reusable ideas.
- francovp ceo-any-cli (625e1df, 7685466) includes #311, but its OpenCode half is V1-only: `--model`, the `chat.message` hook, the TUI `model.json` state file, a prompt-ready screen regex, and a remote MCP entry without `oauth: false`. Its CLI-neutral parts are worth keeping: the `nextSession` CLI switch, the CEO CLI setting, per-CLI office tool names, read-only office file tools with realpath containment, and the Codex CEO read-only flags. It also has the `effectiveModel` bug that rejects Codex `ollama/...` models.

The upstream OpenCode touchpoints, each with file:line, are listed in the facts. Paths are relative to C:/Users/peti/dev/kingpeti/VisualFactory/.claude/worktrees/repo-audit-ai-factory-74210e. My notes and downloaded docs are in C:/Users/peti/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c968d675ef2f985c/23326b94-69a1-40d9-887d-ac86b5b528d8/scratchpad/oc2docs.

There is a conflict to resolve before the D-005 work: the project CLAUDE.md SAFETY section still says "don't add hooks, permission rules or sandboxes that refuse tool calls", while D-005 asks for exactly that. Which one wins needs your decision.
research.recommendation:
Hand-port a V2-only integration onto 157efde in small PRs. Use droidsembly's design as the reference: native V2 config, `--standalone`, an office-assigned `ses_` ID passed with `--session`, plugin options instead of environment variables, and `session.execution.*` events. Keep the diff as small as mysteryreloaded's. Drop all V1 code paths (D-001) and take nothing from Calel33's dual-version code.

Landing order:
1. A version check that refuses OpenCode below 2.x with the install command.
2. The V2 launch and plugin.
3. Migrate the #311 local models to V2 providers. Ollama and LM Studio use V2's built-in discovery; llama.cpp and oMLX become custom openai-compatible providers.
4. CEO on any CLI, part 1: francovp's CLI-neutral and Codex parts plus the `effectiveModel` fix, with an OpenCode CEO refused for now.
5. CEO on OpenCode 2: office MCP as a remote server with `oauth: false` and `codemode: false`; deny edit, shell, subagent and question.
6. D-005 rules for OpenCode: ordered `permissions` deny rules plus a plugin `permission.hook('evaluate')`.

OpenCode 2 must land before CEO-on-any-CLI. Otherwise francovp's OpenCode-1 code lands only to be rewritten, and the two PRs collide in the same `launchArgs` branch. Before step 6, resolve the conflict between the CLAUDE.md SAFETY section and D-005. Before merging step 2, run it once by hand against a real OpenCode 2.3.0 on Windows.

facts.claim: The latest OpenCode is 2.3.0, published on npm as @opencode/cli on 2026-11-13. 2.0.0 was published on 2026-09-11. There were 48 releases from 2.0.0 to 2.3.0.
GitHub release v2.3.0 of anomalyco/opencode was published 2026-11-13 (default branch: dev). The npm package's repository is github.com/anomalyco/opencode.
The V1 line is still published as opencode-ai (latest 1.19.5, 2026-10-28). @opencode-ai/sdk and @opencode-ai/plugin are also at 1.19.5.

@opencode/cli 2.3.0 exposes two bins, `opencode` and `opencode2`, both pointing to bin/opencode.exe, with per-platform optionalDependencies including windows-x64 and windows-arm64 and a postinstall script.

V2 install options: npm install -g @opencode/cli, the curl script at https://opencode.ai/v2/install, or brew anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2. Windows package managers are not supported; standalone Windows zips exist. V1 and V2 both use the `opencode` command, so a package-managed V1 must be removed first.
OpenCode is not installed on this machine, so no --version or --help was run.
facts.source: `where opencode` → 'Could not find files'; `which opencode` → not found

facts.claim: The V2 full-screen TUI (root command) accepts --standalone, --server, --auto, a directory argument, --continue/-c, --session/-s ('Session ID to continue, or to create if it does not exist') and --prompt. It has no --model flag.

`opencode run` (headless) accepts --model in the form provider/model#variant, plus --agent, --format json, --session, --continue, --fork, --file, --title, --archived, --thinking, --auto, --standalone and --server. `opencode mini` accepts --model, --prompt and --session.

In V2 the TUI model comes from config: the top-level `model` key or `agents.<id>.model`, in the form provider/model#variant. A fork observed that passing --model to the 2.1.3 TUI makes the CLI exit at once with ShowHelp.
facts.source: https://opencode.ai/v2/migrate-v1.md (Agents and modes); mysteryreloaded 8dc1d0c commit message

facts.claim: By default every V2 client connects to one shared background server per user, which owns sessions, configuration, permissions and tool execution. --standalone runs a private server instead.
The standalone server is spawned as a child process with `--stdio --port 0` and a random OPENCODE_PASSWORD.
A --session ID that does not exist yet becomes the ID of the session the first prompt creates. Session IDs only need to start with 'ses'.
The TUI opens a resumed --session with the --prompt text as its startup prompt.
V2 still loads OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT as an inline config document.
V2 still accepts most V1 config fields and normalizes them in memory. The intended breaking changes are only: plugins, the server API, and tui.json moving to cli.json.
facts.source: https://opencode.ai/v2/migrate-v1.md (Breaking changes, Use your existing configuration)

facts.claim: The V2 plugin config key is `plugins`, whose entries are a package or path string or `{ package, options }`. Configured local paths must be directories; a path to a single file is skipped. A plugin can be disabled with a '-<id>' entry.

A V2 server plugin is a default export `{ id, setup(ctx) }`. Plugin.define is the identity function, so an import-free object works. setup may return a cleanup function, and ctx.options carries the plugin's options.

V2 plugins receive events through ctx.event.subscribe(), and the events carry `data`. Relevant public events: session.created (with parentID), session.status (idle, busy, retry), session.idle (deprecated), session.execution.started, succeeded, failed (with error) and interrupted (with reason), session.text.ended (with text), session.tool.called, success and failed, session.step.ended (with cost and tokens), session.usage.updated (with cost and tokens).
`session.error` is not on the V2 public event stream: it is absent from the session, status and legacy event definitions.
facts.source: packages/schema/src/session-event.ts; session-status-event.ts; v1/legacy-event.ts; event-manifest.ts:72-83 (legacy events only in Definitions, line 95)

facts.claim: V2 plugin hooks include ctx.tool.hook('execute.before' and 'execute.after'), ctx.permission.hook('evaluate') (may set effect to deny; a configured deny is final), ctx.shell.hook('create.before'), and ctx.session.hook for prompt, context and model.request.
facts.source: https://opencode.ai/v2/build/plugins/server.md (Hooks: Permissions, Shell, Tools); build/plugins/migrate-v1.md hook table

facts.claim: The V2 MCP config sits under mcp.servers.<name>. A local server is { type: 'local', command[], cwd, environment, disabled, codemode, timeout }. A remote server is { type: 'remote', url, headers, oauth (false to disable; OAuth is the default), disabled, codemode }. `enabled` became `disabled`. Code Mode is on by default, and tools are named <server>_<tool>.
facts.source: https://opencode.ai/v2/mcp-servers.md (Config, Local, Remote, Names, Permissions); migrate-v1.md (MCP servers)

facts.claim: V2 permissions are an ordered `permissions` array of { action, resource, effect: allow, ask or deny }, where the last match wins and no match means ask. The actions include read, edit, glob, grep, shell (bash in V1), subagent (task in V1), skill, question, webfetch, websearch, external_directory and <server>_<tool>. Per-agent rules live in agents.<id>.permissions. A shell scanner covers Bash, POSIX sh and PowerShell.
--auto auto-approves permissions that are not explicitly denied. The default base policy allows everything, and only .env reads ask. external_directory is allowed by default in V2.

Policies (`policies`, e.g. tool.use 'shell:git push *' deny) only ever tighten and override ask decisions and saved approvals. Precedence is documented for managed, system, Console, global and project files, but not for OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT.

The V2 updater reads its policy only from the global config files (config.json, opencode.json, opencode.jsonc) and defaults to 'notify'. `autoupdate: false` in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT therefore has no effect.

V2 discovers Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) and LM Studio (127.0.0.1:1234/v1) as built-in providers `ollama` and `lmstudio`; settings.baseURL overrides the address. Other OpenAI-compatible servers need a custom provider: { package: '@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible', settings: { baseURL }, models }.
V2 reads only AGENTS.md (global, then upward from the workspace) followed by the configured `instructions`. It has no CLAUDE.md fallback.
Usage and cost data in V2: cost in USD and token counts on session.step.ended and session.usage.updated events, `opencode stats --cost --json`, and `opencode session export`.

Upstream starts OpenCode with V1-only arguments: `--auto`, a `--model` flag (mapped for local models), `--session`, `--prompt`. Its OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT uses V1 keys: `plugin` (a file URL), `instructions`, `autoupdate: false`, a `permission` object, a V1 provider entry, and `mcp.playwright` with enabled: true.

The upstream OpenCode plugin is a V1 single-file default async function using the `event` hook (session.created, session.idle, session.error with props.info) and client.session.messages. cliRunner writes it as a single file, bin/opencode-plugin.mjs.

open_risks: No real OpenCode 2 was run (it is not installed here). The exact `--version` output, whether `--prompt` auto-submits on a new `--session` ID, and Windows behaviour (npm .cmd shim pointing at bin/opencode.exe, the standalone child server dying under taskkill /T) are only likely. Run one manual demo-free check against 2.3.0 before merging the V2 launch PR.

Repo-level opencode.json can weaken office enforcement: a later `allow` rule wins (last match), and a '-cubefarm' plugins entry disables the office plugin. Where OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT sits in permission and policy precedence is undocumented. A disabled plugin also stops TurnComplete, so the office must treat a missing turn end as a visible failure.
The CLAUDE.md SAFETY section forbids hooks, permission rules or sandboxes that refuse tool calls, which conflicts with D-005. The owner has to decide which wins before the enforcement PR.

V2 changes fast (48 releases from 2.0.0 to 2.3.0 in about 9 weeks). session.idle is already deprecated, and event names or plugin APIs may move. Pin a tested minimum, re-check events on each bump, and rely on session.execution.* rather than session.idle.

V1 and V2 both install `opencode`, and opencode-ai 1.19.5 is still the `latest` of the V1 package, so managers may have V1 on PATH. The version check covers it; trying the `opencode2` bin name as a fallback is optional.
Persisted agents may hold V1 OpenCode session IDs. V2 `--session` silently creates a new empty session with an unknown ID, so drop non-`ses_cubefarm` OpenCode resume IDs on state load.

research.summary:
Upstream enforces nothing. It approves every tool call on every CLI, and the office rules exist only in prompts:
- Claude Code: the PreToolUse hook always answers allow (server/cliRunner.ts:188-189, returned at :446 and :667), the sessions run in acceptEdits mode (server/clis.ts:252-253), and the SDK's canUseTool is allowAll (server/agentRunner.ts:126,367-368).
- Codex runs with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (server/clis.ts:282-284). Its hook script always prints {} (server/clis.ts:433-441), and the office answers the "Hooks need review" prompt with "Continue without trusting" (server/cliRunner.ts:912-924).
- OpenCode gets edit, bash and webfetch all set to allow, plus --auto (server/clis.ts:294,301).
- Cloud Box agents get the same local allow answer (server/boxHelpers.ts:56-57).
- The CEO is the one exception: Bash, PowerShell and NotebookEdit are disallowed for it (server/clis.ts:246, server/agentRunner.ts:347-348). It is still allowed Write and Edit inside the clones.

What the current CLIs offer for enforcement:
- Claude Code: PreToolUse hook decisions (allow, deny, ask, defer) and settings deny rules that a hook cannot override. --settings ranks above the repository's own settings. Its OS sandbox does not run on native Windows and covers only shell commands. HTTP hooks fail open unless onFailure:"block" is set, which needs v2.1.295. The SDK installed in this checkout bundles 2.1.283.
- Codex 0.166: PreToolUse deny works for shell, exec_command, apply_patch and MCP tools. Hooks the manager has not trusted are skipped unless --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust is passed.
  - workspace-write makes .git read-only, so commits fail, and it turns the network off by default.
  - The Windows sandbox has three implementations:
    - MXC: needs Windows 11 24H2. This office runs Windows 10 19045.
    - elevated: needs admin setup.
    - unelevated: weaker network isolation.
- OpenCode 2: a `permissions` array of {action, resource, effect} where the last match wins, per-agent overrides, and policies (`tool.use`) that a repository cannot loosen. Its plugins can deny through permission.hook("evaluate"). It has no OS sandbox.

Reference forks:
- localloop-pro enforced-git-safety has the right pieces: PreToolUse deny, a Codex hook that passes the office's decision back, an OpenCode deny map and a pre-push hook. But it has two overlapping regex implementations, uses the OpenCode V1 config shape, and its per-worktree core.hooksPath turns off the repository's own git hooks.
- francovp ceo-any-cli has a working read-only CEO for each CLI. Codex: --sandbox read-only, -a never, shell_tool off, office MCP approve. OpenCode: edit, bash and task denied.

The recommended design stacks five layers:
1. A pure policy core.
2. Static rules in each CLI.
3. The office's decision hook in each CLI.
4. A guard that works the same for every CLI: a pre-push hook installed through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, which chains the repository's own hooks, plus withholding GitHub and git credentials from QA, reviewers, analysis tasks and the CEO.
5. A check that warns when the default branch has no GitHub ruleset.

OS sandboxes are used only where they don't break the role: Codex read-only sandbox for reviewers, analysis tasks and the CEO.
research.recommendation:
Use option C, layered enforcement. Use one pure policy and one small adapter per CLI. Add a git guard and credential withholding that work for every CLI. Use sandboxes only where they fit Windows and the role. Ship it as the small PRs in the plan, in order P0, P1, P2, P5, P4, P3, then P6 once the OpenCode 2 migration (D-001) has landed. P7 is optional.

Rules kinds (RulesKind):
- builder: the developer and the fixer (legacy tasks issue and fix inside cubefarm.development, ADR-007).
- tester: QA.
- read-only: the independent reviewer (artifact.review) and the analysis task (ai.task).
- ceo.

Each session's kind comes from rulesFor(role, task). Workflow executors pass `rules` explicitly.

Policy matrix (what each kind may not do, and how each CLI enforces it):

builder: no push to the default branch, no force push, no remote branch deletion, no --no-verify, no `-c core.hooksPath`, no gh pr merge or merge endpoints through gh api, no gh pr review, and no file-tool writes outside the worktree and the machine temp folder.
- Claude Code: acceptEdits, plus the office's PreToolUse deny on both runtimes (terminal and SDK hooks.PreToolUse; canUseTool alone is skipped when someone's allow rules approve the call). --settings adds permissions.deny for both the Bash() and PowerShell() forms, and disableAllHooks:false so a repository cannot switch the office's hooks off. After P3: onFailure:"block" on PreToolUse and blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories.
- Codex: keep bypass mode. workspace-write makes .git read-only, so commits would fail. Add the office hook with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, and check apply_patch paths in the hook.
- OpenCode 2: a permissions array (shell denies, external_directory deny), plus a plugin evaluate hook that asks the office.
- Every CLI: the pre-push guard.
- Prompt-only: shell writes outside the worktree, network, running gh by its full path or from a script, pushing to another agent's branch, and a fixer opening a new PR.

tester: no git commit or push, no GitHub writes, and nothing on GitHub at all, since the office posts QA's report (server/prompts.ts:123).
- Every CLI: credentials withheld. GH_CONFIG_DIR points to an empty office folder, GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are removed, credential.helper is reset through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
- Every CLI: commit, push and gh write denials through the same hook and rules as builder.
- Codex: stays in bypass mode with hooks. On Windows, MXC stops detached dev servers and the legacy sandboxes need admin setup. A workspace-write option with network on can come later for macOS and Linux.
- Prompt-only: editing the code under test. Writing probe files is allowed, and the next task's reset --hard discards them.

read-only: no file-tool writes outside the machine temp folder, no git writes, no GitHub writes, credentials withheld.
- Claude Code: hook plus deny rules. Bash stays, with git and gh write denials, because there is no sandbox on native Windows.
- Codex: --sandbox read-only -a never instead of bypass, plus hooks.
- OpenCode 2: edit denied except the temp folder, shell denies, plugin.

ceo: no shell, writes only to its notes file, actions only through office MCP tools, credentials withheld.
- Claude Code: today's disallowed tools, plus a hook that limits Write and Edit to the notes file.
- Codex and OpenCode: francovp's flags, after the ceo-any-cli cherry-pick. Codex: read-only sandbox, -a never, shell_tool off, office MCP approve. OpenCode: edit, shell and subagent denied, with notes saved through the office's save_notes tool.

Network: prompt-only for every kind on Windows. The exception is a Codex read-only sandbox, where one runs.

Git guard, the same for every CLI:
- An office-owned hooks folder (<SWARM_HOME>/bin/git-hooks) is set with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT in the session environment. That ranks above every config file, so husky's local core.hooksPath cannot remove it. Only `git -c` can, and the hook layer denies that.
- The pre-push hook refuses the default branch, deletions and non-fast-forward pushes, then runs the repository's own pre-push.

OpenCode V2 permissions are a `permissions` array of {action, resource, effect}, with actions such as shell, edit, read, webfetch, external_directory and subagent. Per-agent rules go under agents.<id>.permissions and are added after the global ones.
OpenCode has no OS sandbox: its shell runs with the host user's full filesystem, process and network access.

An OpenCode V2 server plugin can deny a call through ctx.permission.hook("evaluate") by setting effect to deny with a message. A deny in the config is final and never reaches the hook. Local plugin paths in the V2 config must be directories.

verification.corrections:
Option C (layered: pure policy, per-CLI adapters, git guard, credential withholding) still holds. These points must change before it ships:

1. Version gating is understated. The office runs the Claude Code bundled with the SDK (2.1.283; server/clis.ts:79-108, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json:91), not the 2.1.316 on PATH. onFailure:"block" (2.1.295+) and blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories (2.1.314+) are unusable until the SDK is bumped. Until then the hook fails open, so the static permissions.deny in --settings is the only layer that does not depend on the office answering. Name the SDK bump explicitly as the prerequisite of whichever PR turns these on.

2. Mods are a gap. Per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions ('Precedence among rules, hooks, and mods'), a mod the manager installed that handles tool.check can approve calls that deny rules or PreToolUse hooks refuse, unless there are managed settings or a Team/Enterprise login. Agents load the manager's setup, so this applies. Investigate the SDK `managedSettings` option, which exists in 0.3.283 (sdk.d.ts:2210-2238) and is filtered restrictive-only. Unverified: whether that parent tier counts as 'managed' for the mod rule, and whether the CLI has a `--managed-settings` flag (it is referenced only in sdk.d.ts:8511 and is absent from `claude --help`).

3. The git-guard claim 'Only git -c can remove it' is wrong. Per git-config docs (installed Git 2.33), GIT_CONFIG_COUNT is overridden by `git -c`, which is GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, and an agent can set either variable in its own command (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 git push`; an empty value counts as 0). The deny layer must also refuse commands that set GIT_CONFIG_*. The gh api deny list must cover git/refs and contents write endpoints, not only merge endpoints. Pushes can also go through libgit2 or other tools. Present the guard as an accident-catcher. The GitHub ruleset stays the only real control.

4. Credential withholding is not a boundary on native Windows, and it misses SSH. This machine uses credential.helper=manager-core (system gitconfig) and gh's token in the keyring, which any shell can read back (for example `git -c credential.helper=manager-core credential fill`, or by clearing GH_CONFIG_DIR). A floor can use the user's own folder, whose origin may be SSH (workspace.ts:28, :842-843), and credential.helper does nothing there. Add GIT_SSH_COMMAND to a refusing command for tester, read-only and ceo, and list 'restoring credentials' as prompt-only.

5. QA does read GitHub. qaPrompt.ts:58 asks QA to 'confirm GitHub's checks are green on the new head', and prompts.ts:120 suggests a fresh merge, which needs a fetch. Reword both in the tester PR to use the checks line the office already provides.

6. Codex hooks fail open on error or timeout, and apply_patch exposes only the patch text in tool_input.command (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks). Run the policy check inside the hook script itself rather than in a round trip to the office, and parse '*** Update/Add/Delete File:' paths from the patch. The .git read-only claim for workspace-write is supported only by third-party sources and a mirrored Codex commit (#1765), not official docs: unverified. The Windows sandbox claims (MXC stopping detached dev servers, admin setup for the legacy sandboxes) are also unverified. That makes '--sandbox read-only' for the read-only kind on Windows unproven: test it before shipping.

7. The OpenCode 2 'plugin evaluate hook' is unverified. No official V2 doc names one. The official V2 facts:
   - `permissions` is an array, the last match wins, and no match falls back to ask, which hangs an unattended agent. Put a catch-all allow first and the denies after it.
   - external_directory is allowed by default.
   - A `policies` hard-deny layer exists that 'turns allow or ask into deny' (https://opencode.ai/v2/policies.md). That fits enforcement better than a plugin hook. Whether policies passed via OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT outrank project config is unverified.

8. Cloud (Box) agents are missing from the matrix. Their hook allows locally (boxHelpers.ts:56-58), so the policy must be built into the Box hook script, and the git-guard env and hooks folder must be installed in the Box. Boxes run Linux, where Claude Code's sandbox is supported, so sandboxing is an option there that the plan currently skips.

research.recommendation:
Fix the real gaps first, in small PRs, and leave routes that already validate well alone until they are touched (D-004 says the rest "migrate over time").

1. The helper. Move the existing parse<T>(schema, value) from index.ts:199-203, unchanged, into a new server/restInput.ts. It throws HttpError(400) with messages like "field: message; ...", and uses "request" when the problem is the whole body. Routes pass `req.body ?? {}` only when every field is optional. Otherwise an undefined body becomes a clean 400 instead of today's 500.

2. Where schemas live. Put them in server/restInput.ts next to the helper, because index.ts cannot be imported by tests: it awaits swarm.init() and starts listening when imported. One-line schemas with no rules may stay inline at the route, as index.ts:210-258 already does. Do not put them in shared/ for now: the client imports shared/outside, shared/notify and shared/cloud at runtime (store.ts:5-7), so zod there would ship to every browser, including phones in pocket mode. The client keeps its own request types in api.ts.

3. What zod checks. Shape, types, enums and generous abuse caps only. The limits users can actually hit stay as Swarm slices: name 24 chars, approve/reject note 400, mission 4000, CEO message 4000. That way nothing typed today starts failing. Fields that a tested pure parser already owns (cleanStyle, parsePreviewPatch, parsePongResult, the settings sub-sanitizers, parseWebhook, checkSubscription, parseRange) are typed z.unknown() in the schema and handed to that parser, so there is one source of truth.

4. Unknown keys. Use z.object, which strips unknown keys as the routes effectively do today, not z.strictObject. Open tabs survive the office's self-update, and the client sends spread nested objects.

5. Order:
   - PR1: helper plus a merge method enum. This closes the flag injection.
   - PR2: agent and team-change routes.
   - PR3: settings and setup.
   - PR4: GitHub/disk identifiers and issues.
   - PR5: the rest, only when touched.
   PR2-PR4 are independent once PR1 lands.

Every rule that depends on state stays in Swarm: 404/409 on requests, the floor cap, CLI installed, box+opencode, assign's busy/deps/holder checks, the settings clamps and cross-field rules, doctor per-finding fixes, demo-only gates, sendBackPatch, checkCloseIssue and progress rules.

Conflict for the owner to confirm: D-004 says "zod at the route", while the codebase's established pattern is tested lenient sanitizers that silently drop bad values. Some of those sanitizers also clean old state files (shared/looks.ts:42-45). My suggested resolution is zod on the outside for shape and the sanitizer on the inside for rules. That turns some silent drops into 400s, which matches your rule 12 ("fail visibly").

open_risks: Zod does not enforce 'no merging by agents' (D-005). With --host, anyone on the LAN can too (index.ts:360-363). This needs a D-005 item, for example a manager-only token or an origin check. That agents know the URL is likely; it was not tested.

Possible CSRF: body-less POSTs are 'simple' cross-site requests. POST /api/repos/<id>/pulls/<n>/merge with no body defaults to squash. Whether current browsers' local-network protections block this was not tested. The fix (an Origin or custom-header check) is outside zod.

research.summary:
ADR-006: the workflow MVP needs little from storage: per-run event logs with idempotency keys, immutable hashed artifacts, append-only approvals, one writer process and low volume. Node 22 can't provide this cleanly with node:sqlite. In the 22.x line it is unflagged since 22.13.0 but still Stability 1.1 "Active development", and it only became a release candidate without the warning in 24.15.0. Its class was renamed DatabaseSync -> Database in 26.11.0. Native drivers bring Windows build risk to `npx cubefarm`. Append-only JSONL matches the codebase's existing persistence (temp+rename JSON and NDJSON) and needs no engines change. Hosted mode will want Postgres anyway, behind the same WorkflowStore port.

ADR-008: today nothing protects any mutating route or websocket. There are no Host, Origin or Sec-Fetch checks. /ws/term types into agent CLIs. Local agents get the office URL in their hook config and can POST /api/requests/:id/approve or /api/repos/:repo/pulls/:n/merge with curl. #310 serves agent-built preview apps under /preview/<port>/ on the office's own origin, so no browser-side check can tell them apart from the manager's UI. Also, the manual merge path does not bind to the head SHA the manager saw.

Recommendation: record a local-manager attestation from a paired device. Bind each approval to the subject hash (artifact sha256 or PR head SHA) and to the run's pinned definition hash, with compare-and-set on approve and a re-check in the merge gate. Protect the endpoint with three things: a ported request boundary, a hashed-at-rest device credential, and moving the preview gateway to its own origin. On native Windows, which is the primary platform, agents run unsandboxed as the same OS user with the manager's gh login. Local approvals there are an attestation, not a security boundary, until D-005 enforcement lands.
research.recommendation:
ADR-006: choose (c), append-only JSONL. Use one file per run at <SWARM_HOME>/workflows/runs/<runId>.jsonl (a demo- prefixed folder in demo mode, like config.ts:48). Each line is an event { seq, at, type, key }. Idempotency keys are unique per run and indexed in memory at load, uncapped (ledger.ts caps its `seen` keys at 600, which would not be safe for external side effects). Append with fs.open('a') and write. fsync (FileHandle.sync) intent and approval events before any external side effect. On load, a torn last line is truncated and logged. A bad line in the middle marks the run corrupt and the UI shows it, so nothing is skipped silently. Artifacts are immutable files named by their sha256, written through journal.ts's writeAtomic (export it, don't copy it). Keep the WorkflowStore type from ARCHITECTURE.md but ship only jsonStore.ts: no sqliteStore.ts. Demo mode uses the same store, so no fake is needed. Backup and export means copying the folder. Engines change: none. Keep "node": ">=22" (package.json:31-33) and MIN_NODE = 22 (bin/cubefarm.js:12). If node:sqlite is ever chosen, it needs "node": ">=24.15.0" (release candidate, no warning) plus a minor-version check in bin/cubefarm.js:49. ">=22.13.0" also works but accepts an experimental API with a warning on 22.x. Revisit when hosted mode arrives (add a Postgres adapter, not SQLite) or when the 2D dashboard (D-002) needs cross-run queries that an in-memory index can't serve.

ADR-008:
(1) Identity: actor = { kind: 'manager', deviceId, channel: 'desktop' | 'pocket' } | { kind: 'auto', rule }, with attestation 'local-manager' (D-003). No usernames or IPs. This extends today's decidedBy 'manager' | 'auto' (shared/types.ts:566).
(2) Binding: subject = { artifact sha256 } | { repo, pr, headSha } | { teamChangeId }, plus runId, stageRunId and definitionHash. The run's pinned definition hash is the policy version, so there is no separate counter. The approve body carries the hash or SHA the UI showed, and the server answers 409 if it no longer matches. The merge gate (mergeStep, server/mergeGate.ts:43) re-checks before merging and refuses with approval_missing or approval_stale (ADR-007). The merge then passes the approved SHA to gh --match-head-commit (github.ts:208). Fix the manual merge path to do the same (swarm.ts:1921-1924 passes no SHA today). Approvals are append-only events in the run log and single-use.
(3) Protection, in three parts:
(a) Port-adapt localloop-pro's request boundary to HTTP, /ws and /ws/term. Allowlist = loopback + HOST interfaces + the officeUrl host + the Vite port in dev. On unsafe methods, require Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin (refuse same-site: other loopback ports count as same-site) and a matching Origin when present. Also require a custom X-Cubefarm-Request header (client api.ts:16 and mic.ts:457 add it). /api/hooks|mcp/:token stay exempt. Send frame-ancestors 'self'.
(b) Require a manager device credential on every unsafe /api route and on /ws/term input. Pairing uses a one-time alphanumeric code opened by bin/cubefarm.js / scripts/office.mjs as #pair=… and printed on the console. Other devices pair from Settings -> Devices. The result is an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, and secrets.json stores only its sha256.
(c) Move the #310 gateway to its own listener and port (opt-in SWARM_PREVIEW_PORT), so preview code is cross-origin to the office. Tailscale users serve that port too.
Later, for hosted mode: OIDC user id and role replace the device. RBAC with approver ≠ author, and agents' service identities can never approve. Previews move to a separate registrable domain, because cookies are not isolated by port. Optional WebAuthn step-up on merge approvals. Agents get a separate least-privilege GitHub identity behind a ruleset that restricts default-branch updates.

options.name: ADR-006 (a) node:sqlite (built-in)
options.pros: No dependency or native build: it ships inside Node. Real SQL transactions (exec BEGIN/COMMIT, isTransaction), UNIQUE constraints and sqlite.backup() (22.16.0+). esbuild (node: prefix external on platform node) and Vitest 5 / Vite 8.3.1 (node:sqlite kept as a prefixed builtin) already handle the import.
options.cons: In the supported 22.x line it is Stability 1.1 with the experimental warning. A clean floor is >=24.15.0, which drops Node 22 LTS users of an npm package. The API is still moving: DatabaseSync was renamed to Database in 26.11.0 (DEP0210). Hosted mode will not use SQLite, so this is an intermediate store. The local dev machine runs Node 20.13.1, which has no node:sqlite at all.

options.name: ADR-006 (b) better-sqlite3 or another native driver
options.pros: Mature, fast and synchronous, with full SQLite features and backups. Works on Node 22.
options.cons: It is a native addon. A missing prebuild means a node-gyp build that needs Visual Studio and Python on Windows, and node-gyp can mis-handle spaces in paths. That is a new failure mode for `npx cubefarm`. It is only tested with currently supported Node versions, so every Node major is an install risk. A second native dependency on top of @lydell/node-pty.

options.name: ADR-006 (c) append-only JSONL plus temp+rename artifacts (recommended)
options.pros: It is the codebase's own convention (state.json, journal NDJSON, secrets.json). No engines change and no bundle impact. Works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. Human-readable and diffable, and backup or export means copying the folder. Fits event-sourced runs with one writer process. Demo mode needs no fake.
options.cons: No multi-file transactions: atomicity is per run file only. Cross-run uniqueness and queries are in-memory indexes rebuilt at startup. You have to write torn-tail handling and fsync rules yourself. Grows without bound until finished runs are archived. Two offices on one SWARM_HOME would interleave appends (state.json already has the same risk).

options.name: ADR-006 (d) PGlite (WASM Postgres)
options.pros: Postgres SQL locally, which would carry over to a hosted Postgres. Runs in Node and persists to the filesystem.
options.cons: Under 3 MB gzipped of WASM plus startup cost for a few runs a day. Single-connection behavior is unverified. A new heavy dependency, and overkill for D-003's local single-user MVP.

options.name: ADR-008 (i) request boundary only (Host, Origin, Sec-Fetch, custom header)
options.pros: Small and well understood (OWASP). Closes cross-site CSRF, DNS rebinding and cross-site websocket hijacking of /ws/term. A tested implementation already exists in the localloop-pro fork.
options.cons: Does nothing against same-origin preview pages (#310 gateway) or local agents using curl, which can forge any header. Approvals stay unauthenticated.

options.name: ADR-008 (ii) boundary + paired-device credential + preview gateway on its own origin + subject-hash binding (recommended)
options.pros: Approvals record which paired device approved which exact hash or SHA. A prompt-injected agent can't approve or merge through the documented API, and preview code becomes cross-origin. Maps directly onto hosted mode later: device becomes an OIDC user.
options.cons: Pairing UX for every new browser or phone. Tailscale users have to serve a second port for previews. On native Windows a same-user agent could still steal the browser's cookie store, so it is attestation, not a hard boundary, without D-005 isolation.

options.name: ADR-008 (iii) (ii) + WebAuthn user-verified step-up on merge approvals
options.pros: The only local option that needs a human gesture (Windows Hello or a passkey). A challenge that carries the subject hash defeats same-origin pages, stolen cookies and agents. It is the natural hosted-mode control.
options.cons: Needs a secure context: works on localhost and Tailscale HTTPS, not on plain-HTTP --host LAN access. Needs a verification library or delicate CBOR/COSE code. More UX friction. Better deferred until (ii) ships and hosted mode starts.

facts.claim: node:sqlite was added in v22.5.0 behind --experimental-sqlite. It has not been behind the flag since v22.13.0 / v23.4.0 but is 'still experimental'. The v22 docs (v22.23.5) show Stability 1.1 Active development and the class DatabaseSync.
node:sqlite became a release candidate (Stability 1.2) in v24.15.0 and v25.7.0

PR #61262 'sqlite: mark as release candidate' removes the experimental warning. It shipped in 24.15.0. Node 22.x presumably still prints ExperimentalWarning because its docs still show 1.1 and no v22 backport is listed.
In v26.11.0 the DatabaseSync class was renamed to Database. DatabaseSync is kept as a deprecated alias (DEP0210, documentation-only).
node:sqlite has no dedicated transaction API. Transactions run as SQL through database.exec(), and database.isTransaction reports state. sqlite.backup() exists since v22.16.0 / v23.8.0.
node:sqlite is compiled into the Node binary, so it needs no native addon build on Windows, macOS or Linux
esbuild marks built-in node modules as external on platform 'node'. Any node:-prefixed import is treated as external on platform node since esbuild 0.12.16. The repo uses esbuild 0.28.2.
The server bundle uses platform node, format esm, target node22 and packages 'external' (dependencies stay external)
Vite 8.3.1 (under Vitest 5.0.2) keeps node:sqlite as a prefixed builtin, and @types/node 26.6.3 ships sqlite.d.ts
package.json engines is node >=22. The launcher checks only the major version (MIN_NODE = 22).
The Node on this machine is v20.13.1. That is below engines >=22 and has no node:sqlite.
Swarm state is debounced 1.5 s and written whole as JSON via state.json.tmp + rename, with no EPERM/EBUSY retry
The journal keeps NDJSON files per 10-minute keyframe, rewritten whole every 30 s through writeAtomic. writeAtomic retries rename on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES and is not exported.
The ledger lives inside state.json (Swarm state field `progress`) and is idempotent through `seen` keys capped at SEEN_KEEP = 600
secrets.json is written with mode 0o600 via temp + rename
The architecture forbids storing workflow runs as fields inside state.json
better-sqlite3 is only tested with currently supported Node versions. Windows builds need Visual Studio and Python, and node-gyp may not escape spaces in paths.
PGlite is under 3 MB gzipped, runs in Node and can persist to the filesystem
No Host, Origin or Sec-Fetch check exists on REST routes. express.json applies to all of /api after the gateway and the token callbacks.
Websocket upgrades for /ws and /ws/term have no Origin check, and /ws/term 'input' messages are written straight to the running CLI
POST /api/requests/:id/approve|reject call Swarm.approveRequest/rejectRequest. Requests record decidedBy 'manager' | 'auto' and decidedAt, and nothing binds them except the pending status.
Auto-merge passes the tested SHA (passedSha ?? headSha) to gh pr merge --match-head-commit. The manager's manual merge route passes no SHA, so it merges whatever head is current.
Pocket mode's Approvals merge button calls api.mergePull after a confirm dialog that shows the title but no SHA

The #310 gateway serves preview apps under /preview/<port>/ on the office's own origin. Its service worker ignores navigations, and escapedTo only redirects GET, so a preview page's form POST or a fetch made after unregistering the worker reaches /api as same-origin.
Local agents get the office URL in their CLI config (the hook URL and the CEO's MCP URL)

The office's workflow rules (no pushes to the default branch, no merging) are in agent prompts, not enforced. The project CLAUDE.md still says not to add hooks, permission rules or sandboxes that refuse tool calls.

The Claude Code sandbox covers shell commands only. Hooks, MCP servers and file tools run outside it. Sandboxed commands can't reach localhost servers by default. Reads of credential files are allowed by default. On native Windows commands run unsandboxed.

OWASP: reject unsafe methods with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, and allow same-site only if siblings are trusted. Verify Origin when present; missing headers or Origin null are not evidence of same origin. Disallowing simple content types or requiring a custom header mitigates CSRF.
Since Chrome 142, public origins need a Local Network Access permission to reach loopback. Whether that covers WebSockets, and what other browsers do, is not confirmed.
Upstream recommends Tailscale Serve (`tailscale serve --bg 4317`) for phones, and says --host has no sign-in
Tailscale Serve accepts `--https=<port> <target>`. Whether several listeners coexist, and which Host header reaches the office, is not confirmed.

The prior audit rates localloop-pro's request boundary as port-adapt: imported as is, it breaks --host, Tailscale Serve and the gateway. It rates mgscox's ws-origin-check as port-adapt and the fork's /api/session token as idea-only. It also flags the gateway's same-origin exposure.
The client sends Content-Type application/json only when a body is present. The clip upload is a raw-body POST.
On Windows the launcher opens the browser through cmd.exe start, so a pairing code in the URL must avoid cmd metacharacters
The CEO's office MCP tools include no approve or merge tool, and the manager merges on floors without auto-merge
